gaps.criterion_why: The leaf itself names the whole-cord false pass, and a positive case that cannot catch it does not test the leaf.
gaps.observed: The action stages only 'one hauler crosses the live end cell, one the dead end cell' plus the visitor and constructors at the live end. The expect still claims 'a crossing of any other cell of the cord shocks no one', and the leaf's false_pass names 'shock applied along the whole cord'. A whole-cord build shocks the live-end crossers (pass) and leaves the dead side harmless (pass), so nothing in the scene catches it. Exam e4 walks along the cord only on the dead side.

gaps.criterion_why: A scene should not pass a build its own leaf names as a false pass; sc_cords_slack's different layout and single look does not cover this one's four looks and end cases.
gaps.observed: The expect reads 'strands read greater than zero in every look (the instrument sees cords); unforced == 0'. The leaf lists the false pass 'cords drawn straight between their ends, so nothing bends at all and the bar is met by a taut cord', and its experience rejects 'slack bought with tight wiggles'. A taut build gives strands > 0 and unforced == 0, so it passes. The planted-hairpin control proves only that the tally can see hairpins.

The scene's action reads only 'the tap registry and style picks', and so do the exam cases e7-e9 and c9. Map ids repeat across games, so a stale printed-section key or priced live-wire cell from game 1 could leave game 2's cords unprinted or make its pawns avoid cells that are not live. No scene reads that state.
